preStudy.title: Pre-Study: Check Your Readiness
preStudy.subtitle: Review the fundamental mathematical concepts required to master Quadratic Functions.

cards.title: 1. Polynomial Degrees & Function Types
cards.desc:
The degree of a polynomial in one variable is the highest exponent of $x$ with a non-zero coefficient:
• Degree 0 (Constant Function): $f(x) = c$ → Graph is a horizontal line.
• Degree 1 (Linear Function): $f(x) = ax + b$ ($a \ne 0$) → Graph is an oblique straight line.
• Degree 2 (Quadratic Function): $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$ ($a \ne 0$) → Graph is a smooth curve called a Parabola.

cards.title: 2. Substitution & Negative Sign Mastery
cards.desc:
Evaluating $f(k)$ means replacing every occurrence of $x$ with the number $k$. Beware the sign rule:
• Parentheses Squaring: $(-3)^2 = (-3) \times (-3) = +9$
• Negative Before Squared Term: $-3^2 = -(3 \times 3) = -9$
• Example: For $f(x) = -x^2 + 5$, then $f(-2) = -(-2)^2 + 5 = -4 + 5 = 1$.

cards.title: 3. Expanding Binomial Squares (Perfect Squares)
cards.desc:
Crucial for transitioning between Vertex Form and Standard Form:
$$(x \pm h)^2 = x^2 \pm 2hx + h^2$$ • $(x - 3)^2 = x^2 - 6x + 9$
• $(x + 2)^2 = (x - (-2))^2 = x^2 + 4x + 4$ → Note that $h = -2$!

cards.title: 4. The Cartesian Plane & Vertical Symmetry
cards.desc:
Every vertical line has equation $x = h$. A parabola is perfectly symmetrical about its axis of symmetry:
Points on the curve at equal vertical heights $y$ are equidistant from the axis $x = h$. The midpoint between any two symmetric points gives the $x$-coordinate of the vertex!

diagnosticQuestions.text: 1. What is the degree of the polynomial function $f(x) = x(x - 4) + 7$?
diagnosticQuestions.explanation: Expanding gives $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 7$. The highest exponent of $x$ is 2, so it is a Quadratic Function of Degree 2.

diagnosticQuestions.text: 2. If $f(x) = 1 - x^2$, what is the exact value of $f(-3)$?
diagnosticQuestions.explanation: $f(-3) = 1 - (-3)^2 = 1 - 9 = -8$. Remember that $(-3)^2 = +9$, preceded by the minus sign.

diagnosticQuestions.text: 3. Which expression is the algebraic expansion of $(x - 5)^2$?

realWorldApps.title: Dolphin Leap Trajectory (Page 1)
realWorldApps.desc: During an aquatic performance, a dolphin leaps out of the water along a parabolic path modeled by $f(x) = -0.2x^2 + 2x$, where $x$ is the horizontal distance in meters and $f(x)$ is the height above water. What is the maximum altitude reached by the dolphin?
realWorldApps.svg: Peak Altitude $f(x) = -0.2x^2 + 2x$ • Max Height $= 5\text{ meters}$ at $x = 5\text{ m}$.
realWorldApps.solutionHtml:
Step-by-Step Mathematical Analysis:
1. Identify the quadratic coefficients: $a = -0.2$, $b = 2$, $c = 0$.
2. Since $a < 0$, the parabola opens downward and possesses a maximum value at the vertex.
3. The horizontal distance at maximum height is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex: $$x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{2}{2(-0.2)} = -\frac{2}{-0.4} = 5\text{ meters}$$ 4. Substitute $x = 5$ into $f(x)$ to calculate the maximum altitude: $$f(5) = -0.2(5)^2 + 2(5) = -0.2(25) + 10 = -5 + 10 = 5\text{ meters}$$ Conclusion: The maximum altitude attained by the dolphin is exactly $\mathbf{5\text{ meters}}$ above water level.

realWorldApps.title: Basketball Arc & Hoop Clearance (Page 1)
realWorldApps.desc: A basketball follows the trajectory $f(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 3)^2 + 6$, where $x$ is the horizontal distance from the player in meters and $f(x)$ is the height. If the basket is located at $(7, 3)$, will the ball go through the hoop?
realWorldApps.svg: Trajectory Test $f(7) = -\frac{1}{3}(7 - 3)^2 + 6 = \frac{2}{3} \approx 0.67\text{ m} \ne 3\text{ m}$.
realWorldApps.solutionHtml:
Mathematical Verification (Point on Curve Test):
1. The hoop is located at $(x, y) = (7, 3)$. For the ball to enter the basket, $f(7)$ must equal $3$.
2. Evaluate $f(7)$ using the given vertex form $f(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 3)^2 + 6$: $$f(7) = -\frac{1}{3}(7 - 3)^2 + 6 = -\frac{1}{3}(4)^2 + 6 = -\frac{16}{3} + \frac{18}{3} = \frac{2}{3}\text{ meters} \approx 0.67\text{ m}$$ 3. Compare with the hoop height: $f(7) = 0.67\text{ m} \ne 3\text{ m}$.
Conclusion: No, the ball will not enter the basket; it drops well below the hoop before reaching $x = 7\text{ m}$.

realWorldApps.title: Football Projectile Peak & Flight Time (Page 5)
realWorldApps.desc: A soccer player kicks a ball upward from the ground. Its height $h(t)$ in meters after $t$ seconds is governed by $h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 19.6t$. Find the maximum altitude attained and the time elapsed to reach that peak.
realWorldApps.svg: Peak Flight Apex reached at $t = 2\text{ seconds}$ with maximum altitude $19.6\text{ meters}$.
realWorldApps.solutionHtml:
Step-by-Step Derivation:
1. The quadratic equation is $h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 19.6t + 0$, where $a = -4.9$, $b = 19.6$, $c = 0$.
2. Time to reach maximum height is the vertex $t$-coordinate: $$t = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{19.6}{2(-4.9)} = -\frac{19.6}{-9.8} = 2\text{ seconds}$$ 3. Maximum height reached: $$h(2) = -4.9(2)^2 + 19.6(2) = -4.9(4) + 39.2 = -19.6 + 39.2 = 19.6\text{ meters}$$ 4. Total time in the air until landing ($h(t) = 0$): $t = 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ seconds}$.
Conclusion: The ball reaches its apex of $\mathbf{19.6\text{ meters}}$ exactly $\mathbf{2\text{ seconds}}$ after the kick.

foundation.title: Core Mathematical Foundation: Quadratic Functions & Parabolas
foundation.subtitle: Formal definitions, standard and vertex representations, and geometric properties.

rules.title: Definition & Domain of a Quadratic Function
rules.desc: A quadratic function is a second-degree polynomial function in one variable of the form $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$, where $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \ne 0$. Its domain is the set of all real numbers $\mathbb{R}$. Its geometric graph is a smooth, continuous U-shaped curve known as a Parabola.

rules.title: Standard Form: $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$
rules.desc:
• x-coordinate of the Vertex: $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$.
• y-coordinate of the Vertex: $y = f\left(-\frac{b}{2a}\right)$.
• Axis of Symmetry: Vertical line $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$.
• y-intercept: Point $(0, c)$ since $f(0) = c$.

rules.title: Vertex Form: $f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k$
rules.desc:
• Vertex Point: Exactly $(h, k)$.
• Axis of Symmetry: Vertical line $x = h$.
• Sign Alert: For $f(x) = (x + 3)^2 + 1$, write it as $(x - (-3))^2 + 1$, giving vertex $(-3, 1)$.

rules.title: Orientation & Extrema (Maximum vs Minimum)
rules.desc:
• If $a > 0$: Parabola opens upward (∪); the vertex is a Minimum Point, with minimum value $y = k = f\left(-\frac{b}{2a}\right)$.
• If $a < 0$: Parabola opens downward (∩); the vertex is a Maximum Point, with maximum value $y = k = f\left(-\frac{b}{2a}\right)$.

ideas.flashcardTitle: Graphing & Analyzing Standard Form: $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$
ideas.flashcardText: Follow the 4-step algorithm: (1) Find vertex $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$, (2) Select symmetric $x$-values around the vertex, (3) Construct the table of values, (4) Plot points and draw a smooth parabola.
ideas.ex1Q: Graph the quadratic function $f(x) = x^2 - 2x - 3$. Identify the axis of symmetry equation and find the maximum or minimum value.
ideas.ex1Svg: Precision Plot $f(x) = x^2 - 2x - 3$ • Vertex $(1, -4)$ • Min Value $= -4$.

ex1Steps.text: Identify coefficients: $a = 1$, $b = -2$, $c = -3$. Since $a > 0$, the parabola opens upward.
Find $x$-coordinate of the vertex: $x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-2}{2(1)} = \mathbf{1}$. Axis of symmetry equation is $\mathbf{x = 1}$.
Determine extremum: Since the curve opens upward, the vertex is a minimum point. The minimum value is $\mathbf{-4}$.

ideas.ex1Ans: Axis of Symmetry: x = 1 • Vertex: (1, -4) • Minimum Value: -4
ideas.ex2Q: Graph $f(x) = -x^2 + 6x - 5$. State the vertex coordinates, axis of symmetry, and the maximum value.
ideas.ex2Svg: Downward Parabola $f(x) = -x^2 + 6x - 5$ • Peak Vertex $(3, 4)$ • Max Value $= 4$.
ideas.tryPrompt: Graph the function $f(x) = 3x - x^2$. On your drawing, clearly indicate the axis of symmetry and find the maximum or minimum value. Also verify whether the point $(6, 21)$ lies on the curve.
ideas.trySolution:
Step-by-Step Model Solution:
1. Rewrite in standard form: $f(x) = -x^2 + 3x + 0$, where $a = -1$, $b = 3$, $c = 0$.
2. Vertex x-coordinate: $$x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{3}{2(-1)} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5$$ 3. Vertex y-coordinate (Maximum Value): $$f(1.5) = 3(1.5) - (1.5)^2 = 4.5 - 2.25 = 2.25 = \frac{9}{4}$$ Vertex is $(1.5, 2.25)$. Since $a = -1 < 0$, the parabola opens downward and the maximum value is $2.25$.
4. Axis of Symmetry Equation: $x = 1.5$.
5. Point $(6, 21)$ Verification:
Substitute $x = 6$: $f(6) = 3(6) - 6^2 = 18 - 36 = -18 \ne 21$.
→ Therefore, $(6, 21)$ does not lie on the curve.

ideas.flashcardText: The vertex is directly $(h, k)$ without using formulas! Watch the negative sign inside: $(x - h)$ means $h$ is positive, but $(x + 2)$ means $h = -2$. The vertical line $x = h$ is the axis of symmetry, and $k$ is the maximum or minimum value.
ideas.ex1Q: Graph $f(x) = 5 - 2(x + 1)^2$. State the vertex coordinates, axis of symmetry, and the maximum or minimum value.
ideas.ex1Svg: Vertex Form Graph $f(x) = -2(x + 1)^2 + 5$ • Peak $(-1, 5)$ • Max Value $= 5$.

ex1Steps.text: Rearrange into standard vertex form: $f(x) = -2(x - (-1))^2 + 5$. Here $a = -2$, $h = -1$, $k = 5$.
The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the vertex: $\mathbf{x = -1}$.
Since $a = -2 < 0$, the parabola opens downward and has a maximum value of 5.

ideas.ex2Q: Given $f(x) = 2(x - 3)^2 + 1$. State the vertex and extrema. If the point $(b, 9)$ lies on the parabola, find all possible values of $b$.
ideas.ex2Svg: Two Symmetric Solutions Horizontal line $y = 9$ intersects the parabola at $b = 1$ and $b = 5$.

ex2Steps.text: Since $a = 2 > 0$, the parabola opens upward, giving a minimum value of 1.

ideas.ex2Ans: Vertex: (3, 1) • Min Value: 1 • b = 1 or b = 5
ideas.tryPrompt:
1) Graph $f(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 4$. State the vertex, axis of symmetry, and minimum value.
2) If the point $(-1, m)$ lies on the curve of $g(x) = -(x + 1)^2 + 3$, calculate the value of $m$.
ideas.trySolution:
Part 1: Graphing $f(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 4$:
• Vertex form: $a = 1, h = 2, k = -4$.
• Vertex coordinates: $\mathbf{(2, -4)}$.
• Axis of symmetry: $\mathbf{x = 2}$.
• Since $a = 1 > 0$, the parabola opens upward, giving a minimum value of $-4$.
• Roots ($f(x) = 0$): $(x - 2)^2 = 4 \implies x - 2 = \pm 2 \implies x = 0$ or $x = 4$.

Part 2: Finding $m$ on $g(x)$:
Substitute $x = -1$ into $g(x)$:
$$m = g(-1) = -(-1 + 1)^2 + 3 = -(0)^2 + 3 = 3$$ → The value of $m$ is $\mathbf{3}$ (and $(-1, 3)$ is the maximum vertex of $g$!).

ideas.flashcardTitle: Solving for Unknown Parameters & Geometric Proofs
ideas.flashcardText: Use the conditions of the problem (e.g., degree of polynomial, coordinates of vertex, axis of symmetry, or geometric distance) to set up algebraic equations and solve for unknown constants.
ideas.ex1Q: In the figure, the curve represents $f(x) = x^2 - 2x + k + 1$ with vertex $V$ and intersecting the y-axis at $C$. $A$ is the projection of $V$ on the x-axis ($x = 1$). If $OA = \frac{1}{2} VA$, find the value of $k$ and the coordinates of point $C$.
ideas.ex1Svg: Geometric Relationship $OA = 1$, $VA = -k$. Given $OA = \frac{1}{2} VA \implies 1 = \frac{1}{2}(-k) \implies k = -2$.

ex1Steps.text: Find vertex $x$-coordinate: $x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-2}{2(1)} = 1$. Thus, projection $A$ is at $(1, 0)$, which means the length $\mathbf{OA = 1}$ unit.
Find vertex $y$-coordinate: $f(1) = 1^2 - 2(1) + k + 1 = 1 - 2 + k + 1 = k$. Since $V$ is below the x-axis, length $\mathbf{VA = -k}$.

Find point $C$ ($y$-intercept): Substitute $x = 0$ into $f(x)$:
$$f(0) = 0^2 - 2(0) + k + 1 = k + 1 = -2 + 1 = -1$$

ideas.ex2Q:
1) If $f(x) = (a + 4)x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 6$ is a quadratic function, find $a$.
2) If $x = 2$ is the axis of symmetry of $f(x) = ax^2 + 12x + 7$, find $a$.
ideas.ex2Svg: Algebraic Properties Eliminating cubic term gives $a = -4$ • Equating axis gives $a = -3$.

ex2Steps.text: For $f(x)$ to be a quadratic function, the degree must be strictly 2. Therefore, the coefficient of $x^3$ must vanish: $a + 4 = 0 \implies \mathbf{a = -4}$.

The axis of symmetry formula is $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$. Here $b = 12$, and the axis is given as $x = 2$:
$$-\frac{12}{2a} = 2 \implies \frac{-6}{a} = 2 \implies 2a = -6 \implies \mathbf{a = -3}$$.

ideas.tryPrompt: If $f(x) = x^2 - 10x + k$ is a quadratic function, and the vertex $V$ is at a distance of 13 units from the origin $O(0, 0)$, find all possible values of the constant $k$.
ideas.trySolution:
Step-by-Step Derivation (Distance Formula Integration):
1. Find the vertex coordinates:
• $a = 1$, $b = -10$, $c = k$.
• $x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-10}{2(1)} = 5$.
• $y = f(5) = 5^2 - 10(5) + k = 25 - 50 + k = k - 25$.
Thus, the vertex is $\mathbf{V(5, k - 25)}$.

2. Set up the Distance from Origin $O(0, 0)$ to $V$:
$$d(O, V) = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = 13$$ $$\sqrt{5^2 + (k - 25)^2} = 13$$ 3. Square both sides:
$$25 + (k - 25)^2 = 169$$ $$(k - 25)^2 = 169 - 25 = 144$$ 4. Solve for $k$:
$$k - 25 = \pm \sqrt{144} = \pm 12$$ • Case 1: $k - 25 = 12 \implies \mathbf{k = 37}$
• Case 2: $k - 25 = -12 \implies \mathbf{k = 13}$

Conclusion: The possible values of $k$ are $\mathbf{13}$ and $\mathbf{37}$.

mcqs.q: 1. What are the coordinates of the vertex of the quadratic function $f(x) = 2(x - 3)^2 + 1$?
mcqs.proof: The vertex form is $f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k$. Here $h = 3$ and $k = 1$, so the vertex is directly $(3, 1)$.

mcqs.q: 2. If $(h, k)$ is the vertex of $f(x) = 2x^2 - 8x + 7$, what is the value of $h$?
mcqs.proof: The $x$-coordinate of the vertex is given by $h = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-8}{2(2)} = \frac{8}{4} = 2$.

mcqs.q: 3. What is the point of intersection of the parabola $f(x) = x^2 - 3x - 5$ with the y-axis?
mcqs.proof: To find the y-intercept, set $x = 0$: $f(0) = 0^2 - 3(0) - 5 = -5$. The point is $(0, -5)$.

mcqs.q: 4. What is the minimum value of the quadratic function $f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 14$?
5. If $f(x) = (a + 4)x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 6$ is a quadratic function, then the value of $a$ is:
mcqs.proof: For $f(x)$ to be a quadratic function (degree 2), the coefficient of $x^3$ must be 0: $a + 4 = 0 \implies a = -4$.

mcqs.q: 6. If $x = 2$ is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex of $f(x) = ax^2 + 12x + 7$, then $a = $
7. Which of the following functions has a vertex at $(2, 4)$ and opens upward?
mcqs.proof: Opening upward requires $a > 0$, and vertex $(2, 4)$ requires $h = 2, k = 4$. Thus $f(x) = (x - 2)^2 + 4$.

mcqs.q: 8. The axis of symmetry equation for $f(x) = 5 - (x + 1)^2$ is:
mcqs.proof: The vertex form is $-(x - (-1))^2 + 5$, so $h = -1$. The vertical line of symmetry is $x = -1$.

mcqs.q: 9. If the point $(k, 5)$ lies on the curve $f(x) = x^2 + 1$, then the possible values of $k$ are:
10. The maximum value of the function $f(x) = -(x - 4)^2 + 16$ is:
mcqs.proof: Since $a = -1 < 0$, the parabola opens downward and reaches its maximum value at $y = k = 16$.

mcqs.q: 11. If $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + c$ has a minimum value of $-1$, then $c = $
mcqs.proof: Vertex $x = -\frac{-4}{2} = 2$. Minimum value $f(2) = 2^2 - 4(2) + c = -1 \implies 4 - 8 + c = -1 \implies c = 3$.

mcqs.q: 12. The parabola $f(x) = 2x^2 + 8$ has its vertex at:
mcqs.proof: Here $b = 0$, so $x = -\frac{0}{2(2)} = 0$. Then $f(0) = 8$. The vertex is on the y-axis at $(0, 8)$.
